requirement:
A definition's reference set MUST consist of its current incoming `{impl}` and
`{test}` edges under {cite}`requirements.references.targets` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: for each edge, its role and the file and
outline selector of the node the reference belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, or of the anchored file or
node, and, for a fenced reference in a source outside the book, the words of
its body under the word rule of {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
`{cite}` references MUST NOT contribute. The reference-set digest MUST be
the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of those entries in sorted order,
so it does not depend on line numbers or on the order references are found.
Authoring MUST record the digest of the reference set it supplied, and
validation MUST recompute it and report a changed reference set as stale
evidence. Adding or removing an `{impl}` or `{test}` reference or anchor,
changing its role, editing its commentary, or moving it to a different node
MUST therefore make the evidence stale even when no recorded input changed; moving a reference within
the node it belongs to MUST NOT.
rationale:
**Judgment:** the implementation and tests satisfy `requirements.ci.reference_set`.

**Implementation**
- `reference_set_digest` (src/evidence.rs) builds the set from exactly the `{impl}` and `{test}` references naming the definition. It skips `{cite}` and any other reference kind.
- Each reference contributes its role, its file, and the selector of its owning outline node. The node comes from `Outline::owner_at_line`, which uses the comment-run ownership of `outline_comments`.
  - Plain-text files and files that cannot be outlined contribute the root node.
  - Line numbers are never encoded, so moving a reference within its node leaves the digest unchanged.
  - Moving it to another node changes the selector, so the digest changes.
- Each declaration anchor contributes its role, file and selector.
- A fenced reference outside the book also contributes the whitespace-split words of its body. In-book commentary is excluded because it is already part of the declaration text, which the requirement allows.
- Entries are sorted. The hash input is length-prefixed (entry count, then each field), which makes the encoding unambiguous. The result is lowercase-hex SHA-256 and does not depend on discovery order.
- Authoring records the digest.
  - `AssessmentSources::prepare` computes it and `authoring::record` writes it.
  - `add_definition_inputs` and `update_inputs` in src/add_input.rs record it too. A change resets the determination to false for reassessment.
- Validation recomputes the digest in `validate_references` and reports "reference set changed" when it differs from the recorded one. `validate_evidence_file` checks that the recorded value is a lowercase SHA-256 hex string, and a missing field is also reported.
- All of this code carries `{impl}` markers for the requirement. `reference_set_digest_for` and the `SourceReference` and `ReferenceSetEntry` types are marked too.
- I found no unspecified behaviour in the marked code. The `origin` field is part of the encoding but is an internal detail of the entry encoding.

**Tests**
- `reference_set_digest_tracks_impl_and_test_edges_by_node` covers these cases:
  - the digest is deterministic;
  - unrelated lines, line moves within a node, moves within a markdown section, and added `{cite}` references leave it unchanged;
  - adding an `{impl}`, removing one, re-roling it, and moving it to another node each change it, as does a second reference in the same node, a reference in a different file, and a reference added to a markdown section;
  - adding an anchor changes it.
- `fenced_commentary_outside_the_book_contributes_to_the_reference_set` covers reflowed commentary (no change), changed words (change), fenced versus inline form (change), and in-book commentary (ignored).
- `validation_requires_a_current_reference_set_digest` covers the missing, non-string, uppercase and truncated digest failures. It also shows that a new `{impl}` inside a node the inputs already cover makes the evidence stale with no recorded input changed.
- Integration tests cover authoring and add-input:
  - `batch_reauthors_a_false_judgment_when_its_reference_set_changes` shows batch authoring reassesses a stale record and re-records the digest.
  - `add_input_requires_one_target_and_mode_and_resets_changed_records` shows add-input records the digest and resets review when only the reference set changed.
  - The authoring tests check that the bundle's digest equals the validator's and that the record stores it.

**Minor observation:** removing an anchor and changing an anchored node's selector are not tested directly. Anchors feed the same sorted-entry encoding, and anchor addition is tested, so I do not treat this as a gap.

A definition's reference set MUST consist of its current incoming `{impl}` and
`{test}` edges under {cite}`requirements.references.targets` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: for each edge, its role and the file and
outline selector of the node the reference belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, or of the anchored file or
node, and, for a fenced reference in a source outside the book, the words of
its body under the word rule of {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
`{cite}` references MUST NOT contribute. The reference-set digest MUST be
the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of those entries in sorted order,
so it does not depend on line numbers or on the order references are found.
Authoring MUST record the digest of the reference set it supplied, and
validation MUST recompute it and report a changed reference set as stale
evidence. Adding or removing an `{impl}` or `{test}` reference or anchor,
changing its role, editing its commentary, or moving it to a different node
MUST therefore make the evidence stale even when no recorded input changed; moving a reference within
the node it belongs to MUST NOT.
:::{req} targets

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under {cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git` and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
A source item MUST choose its references for each candidate definition by this
procedure, and MAY carry several:
1. If the item is a test or test helper designed to verify the definition, it
MUST use `{test}`.
2. Otherwise, if fulfilling the definition depends on the item, it MUST use
`{impl}`. For code, this means it makes a decision, performs a check,
produces an output, or handles a case the definition specifies. For a type,
this means the definition constrains its shape: fields, variants, serialized
form, or validation.
3. Otherwise, if the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the
definition changes, it MUST use `{cite}`.
4. If the item carries no reference after applying steps 1 to 3 to every
definition, it MUST cite the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, justifying why the item
exists.

:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile
MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text MUST be hashed,
not its delimiter tokens such as `//`, `///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`,
so reflowing it across more or fewer lines does not change the hash. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
